what: Relative L2 error of logits against an independent float64 forward pass, per architecture. Establishes which side of a two-way engine-vs-llama.cpp diff is actually wrong.
method: scripts/arbitrate_logits.py computes a third forward pass in float64 directly from the fixture weights, following llama.cpp's src/models/<arch>.cpp graph order. All three (engine, llama.cpp, float64) run the same token sequence 3,17,42,99,7,61,127,24 through the same synthetic F32 fixtures.
findings: llama.cpp's own forward pass is the LESS accurate of the two by ~1000x. A two-way engine-vs-llama.cpp diff cannot reveal this; it looks like a parity gap when it is the oracle that is drifting.
Cause 1: build_attn_mha casts K and V to GGML_TYPE_F16 before ggml_flash_attn_ext (llama-graph.cpp:2530). Disabling flash attention drops llama/qwen2 from ~5e-4 to ~2e-7.

Cause 2: the KV cache defaults to F16 (llama-context.cpp:3508). Measured to be a no-op on these fixtures once flash attention is off, so it is not a factor here - but it is still a 5e-4-class source on longer contexts where flash attention is not in play.

Cause 3: GGML_GELU_FP16 is #defined unconditionally (ggml-cpu/vec.h:46), so GELU is evaluated by looking up a 64K-entry float16 table keyed on the float16 bits of the input. Modelling that table in the float64 reference reproduces llama.cpp's gpt2 to 1.5e-7, confirming it is the entire residual. It cannot be disabled from outside ggml, which is why gpt2 needs a looser gate against the llama.cpp reference.
consequences: engine/tests/ref_parity.rs now gates on TWO references per arch: <arch>.ref (llama.cpp, proves we compute its function) and <arch>.f64.ref (exact math, the tight gate).
gpt2 has a 2e-3 floor against llama.cpp by necessity, not by slack; its real constraint is the 1e-5 float64 gate.
The F32 parity claim is now ~5e-7, not the ~2e-4 previously reported against llama.cpp.
not_explained: The real Qwen2.5-3B Q4_K_M gap (cos 0.996-0.9993) is NOT explained by any of the three causes above: for a 3B model at 36 layers the float16 shortcuts accumulate far less than the observed disagreement, and quantization error dominates. Still open.
